Restate only the main (public) question.
Compute \(26 \times 43 + 29 \times 14\).

First, calculate \(26 \times 43\):
\[26 \times 43 = 26 \times (40 + 3) = (26 \times 40) + (26 \times 3)\]
\[26 \times 40 = 1040\]
\[26 \times 3 = 78\]
\[26 \times 43 = 1040 + 78 = 1118\]

Next, calculate \(29 \times 14\):
\[29 \times 14 = 29 \times (10 + 4) = (29 \times 10) + (29 \times 4)\]
\[29 \times 10 = 290\]
\[29 \times 4 = 116\]
\[29 \times 14 = 290 + 116 = 406\]

Now, add the results together:
\[1118 + 406 = 1524\]

To verify the main result, let's try an alternative order of operations:
First, calculate \(29 \times 14\) again (which we already know is 406).
Then, calculate \(26 \times 43\) again (which we already know is 1118).
Finally, add these results:
\[1118 + 406 = 1524\]

This confirms our initial calculation.
